links.comparator_used: Standalone AI services (three commercial ICH detection tools) acting alone, versus radiologists who had AI results available as an auxiliary tool
links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy for ICH detection on brain CT (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, diagnostic odds ratio, false positives, missed cases)
links.effect: Sensitivity 98.91% vs 95.91%, specificity 99.83% vs 87.35%, accuracy 99.53% vs 90.11% (p<0.001); diagnostic odds ratio 52,272 vs 162.0 (323-fold); false positives 4 vs 293 (0.17% vs 12.65%); missed ICH 12 vs 45 cases; kappa 0.776
links.tradeoff: AI use was optional, and radiologists may not have used the AI results. The radiologist arm is not a clean test of AI assistance, since it was not compared with radiologists reading without AI. Adding AI findings to radiologist reads could raise false positives from 4 to 297 cases, requiring extra specialist verification and workload and risking alert fatigue.
links.quote: Sensitivity was 98.91% vs. 95.91% for AI, specificity was 99.83% vs. 87.35%, and overall accuracy was 99.53% vs. 90.11%.

design_hint: clinician review of AI outputs (radiologist-in-the-loop second reader)
